name: Bongbong Marcos
role: President of the Philippines (2022–), former senator and congressman
summary: Ferdinand Marcos Jr. governs as a pro-investment, state-active pragmatist: he courts private capital and public-private partnerships while using price ceilings, a state investment fund and expanded health coverage. In foreign policy he keeps a 'friend to all' line but has deepened military cooperation with the United States and Japan and insists on Philippine sovereignty in the West Philippine Sea. On social questions and civil liberties his own record is thin or hedged, so most of those statements are left without a position.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 2023 address he names universal healthcare as a goal and presents wider PhilHealth coverage as the route; the 2024 and 2025 addresses report benefit expansions he ordered.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He states the campaign against illegal drugs continues, aiming to eliminate the trade and calling it a corrosive social curse, with treatment for users; no legal market is proposed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He told Congress it was time to re-examine building nuclear power plants, naming IAEA compliance and small modular reactors, and repeated in 2026 that it is time to revisit nuclear energy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: At the UN he called climate change the greatest threat and demanded industrialised countries immediately cut emissions and fund adaptation, while accepting the Philippines' own share.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He framed climate change as an injustice in which those least responsible suffer most, and called on the high emitters to cut greenhouse gases.

future-generations.rationale: He urged solutions that preserve the planet for succeeding generations and warned that future generations will ask why leaders did not act.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: At the UN he said states must reject the notion of deterrence and reduce the global stockpile of nuclear weapons.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He told the General Assembly to reject nuclear deterrence and cut stockpiles, which rules out keeping weapons because of a nuclear-armed rival.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His 2023 address reports that the police and armed forces are being strengthened and modernised to defend sovereignty, and he proposed an overhaul of the National Defense Act rather than any reduction.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: In his first address he pledged not to preside over any process that gives up even a square inch of Philippine territory, and repeated in 2023 that territorial integrity must be preserved; a pledge, so medium.

right-to-secede.rationale: His inaugural address describes the Philippines as one nation, one indivisible republic, and his 2023 address says the nation must remain intact and inviolable.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He signed an order fixing maximum retail prices for regular and well-milled rice nationwide, citing hoarding, cartel collusion and a price surge, though the order itself notes supply was steady rather than short.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He pushed through and signed a state investment fund that makes strategic and profitable investments in key sectors such as infrastructure, energy and agriculture, directed at national priorities.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: His government widened the US military access agreement by four sites and concluded a reciprocal access agreement with Japan,

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Though he calls his policy friend to all and enemy to none, his government expanded US access to Philippine bases and signed a defence access pact with Japan.

close-ties-china.rationale: His government deepened military ties with the US and Japan, and he cited Chinese actions at sea as a reason for the added access sites.

arbitrator-settles-disputes.rationale: He praised the Law of the Sea convention as a model for states to resolve differences by reason and right, and in 2026 called the 2016 arbitral award final and binding.

uniformed-youth.rationale: He asked Congress to make ROTC mandatory for senior high school students, to train, organise and mobilise them for national defence preparedness.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He told the General Assembly that sustainable development will suffer if existing global economic structures remain unreformed and that knowledge and technology must flow to those lagging behind.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: At the UN he called for a system fair to all peoples including migrants and refugees, and an end to racism and prejudice.
